newsitem.title: JAPAN: FREESTYLE SKIING-BRASSARD WINS WORLD MOGULS TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FREESTYLE SKIING-BRASSARD WINS WORLD MOGULS TITLE.

text.p: Jean-Luc Brassard brushed aside a shoulder injury to win the men's moguls title at the world freestyle skiing championships on Saturday, then made a post-race confession.

The shoulder injury, which he sustained two weeks ago just a day before a World Cup competition in Breckenridge, Colorado, had actually occurred while he was fooling around on the slopes, a detail he had previously thought better to spare his coaches.
The injury prevented him from competing at Breckenridge, although he still leads the World Cup moguls standings, and caused the Canadian team anxious moments before the Nagano championships.
Taped and trussed, Brassard ignored his shoulder discomfort, electrifing the crowd of 6,000 with tight, quick turns and two near-perfect triple jumps on the 260-metre Mount Iizuna slope.
"In the world championships, you squeeze your teeth a little bit more," said Brassard, who scored 27.52 points. "The tape kind of held everything together."
Fellow Canadian Stephane Rochon placed second with 26 points. Jesper Ronnback of Sweden was third with 25.43 points.
Canadian head coach Peter Judge was understanding. "Sometimes as much as we want to put these guys in a bubble and insulate them from all danger, you can't," he said.
The Canadians opted to shift to the right-hand side of the course -- they used the opposite line during qualification rounds -- after deciding that the bottom jump offered a chance for bigger jumps.
"It was a great tactical move," said Judge. "It was a good line and accented their highlights well."
Candice Gilg of France successfully retained her women's moguls title with a score of 24.84 points, with a little help from older brother Youri, a former member of the French national freestyle team.
Gilg said Youri first convinced her to try one of the two jumps she used on Saturday, a gutsy double daffy with skis split to the front and back.
World Cup champion Donna Weinbrecht performed her first-ever triple jump in competition to place second with 24.60 points.
The 31-year-old American, who finished a disappointing seventh at the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics, said she hoped to use her triple jump at the Nagano Games next year .
Germanys Tatjana Mittermayer, World Cup leader in moguls, was third with 24.20 points.
